name: identity-conflict-same-identity-group-move
description: The forbidden shape: a `remove` and a `create` at the SAME identity in one change set. The protocol bans same-identity replacement GLOBALLY — for every uniquely identified element and every uniquely identified nested member — because the semantic differ does not represent relocation, or an in-place change of an immutable field, as a permitted delta: the vocabulary is `create`, `remove` and `update` at an address, and none of those means "the same thing, elsewhere or differently identified". A group move is the instance shown here because `swc.group` is immutable placement metadata and this is the only way it could be written; the `kind` discriminators of `interfaces`, `application_types`, `implementation_types` and `hardware`, and renaming in place run into exactly the same ban.

context.summary: The `examples/basic` model, where `ExampleSWC` is stored under the `example` group. The client wants it under `sensors` instead and states the move the only way the operation set allows: remove it, then create it again with the same name and a different group.

authorization.notes: The scope covers both operations exactly, so the refusal is the identity rule and not the authorization boundary — the same shape as `immutable-field-memory-kind-discriminator.json`. An approved scope can no more make an identity reusable inside one change set than it can make an immutable field writable.

input.intent: Move ExampleSWC from the example group into the sensors group.

value.name: ExampleSWC
value.description: Example software component for testing and demonstration

expected.notes: Why this is a refusal rather than a feature: the current and future semantic differ has no delta entry that represents a relocation, so the pair would reach the review boundary as something other than what was asked for and the user would approve a delta that is not the request. The argument is deliberately not one from snapshot equality — `group` is carried as placement metadata, so the two snapshots differ — nor one from byte equality, since the files differ either way. Refusing the pair at pass B turns a change the review surface cannot express into a stated rejection with an address on it. The ban is global and its consequences are these: relocating an SWC between groups, changing an `interfaces`/`application_types`/`implementation_types`/`hardware` `kind`, and renaming an element or member in place all become unreachable through the protocol, and each stays a user act on the user's own files — edit the YAML, `git mv` for a group — where the trust boundary already puts it. Two shapes stay legal and are the contrast this vector rests on: a `remove` and a `create` at DIFFERENT identities is the rename case (`examples/rename-swc-via-remove-create-and-reference-updates.json`), and a `remove` and a `create` of the same value in a `whole_value` LIST is a multiset operation rather than an identity replacement, because such members are counted rather than uniquely identified (`examples/create-and-remove-duplicate-runnable-events.json`).
